analysisType: Offline AI semantic review of the complete extracted Armstrong day, with explicit context links. Not a live model run or validated mental health assessment.
scope: Voiced requests, decisions and issue reports; four reviewed repair exchanges; two coordination snags; two explicit busy statements; four technical-support exchanges. Counts overlap between KPIs.
dayRationale: Critical landing work and Armstrong’s own description of alarms competing with landing-site observation support a demanding-day interpretation. Today’s demand, repair, coordination and pressure counts exceed the simulated usual ranges used for this demo; captured support responses are within that simulated usual range. The baseline is illustrative, not reconstructed historical data. Transcript volume alone is not a mental health measure.

demand.title: Activation mismatch
demand.interpretation: Reports an unexpected talkback state; later reports a circuit breaker out of position.

demand.title: Radio sender check
demand.interpretation: Checks which channel Collins is transmitting on.

demand.title: Radio channel setup
demand.interpretation: Checks Simplex B, asks Collins to configure Simplex A, then checks A. Grouped as one setup episode.

demand.title: Clock loading and synchronization
demand.interpretation: Requests the clock data and agrees the order for loading it. Follow-up turns are one episode.

demand.title: Timed synchronization mark
demand.interpretation: Coordinates a timed mark and checks receipt.

demand.title: Ephemeris data request
demand.interpretation: Requests T EPHEM via a specified verb/noun sequence.

demand.title: Docked alignment setup
demand.interpretation: Coordinates an alignment and asks for minimum-deadband attitude hold.

demand.title: Alignment angle data
demand.interpretation: Requests NOUN 20 values.

demand.title: Release attitude hold
demand.interpretation: Tells Collins the hold is no longer needed; an explicit change in coordination.

demand.title: Repeat timed measurement
demand.interpretation: Requests NOUN 20 again and restarts the mark. Routine measurement repetition, not counted as confusion.

demand.title: Check angle reception
demand.interpretation: Checks that ground copied the angles.

demand.title: Check associated time
demand.interpretation: Checks that ground has the measurement time.

demand.title: Confirm next alignment command
demand.interpretation: Asks whether to execute VERB 42 now.

demand.title: Check angle copy
demand.interpretation: Checks receipt of torquing angles.

demand.title: Clarify addressee
demand.interpretation: Asks whether the message is to Columbia.

demand.title: Ground viewing configuration
demand.interpretation: Asks about high-gain use before ground checks an indicator.

demand.title: RCS checkout readiness
demand.interpretation: Asks ground whether to begin the RCS checkout.

demand.title: Coordinate timed data display
demand.interpretation: Asks Collins to configure a display for a timed check.

demand.title: Confirm maneuver status
demand.interpretation: Checks whether Collins is maneuvering.

demand.title: Tracking light check
demand.interpretation: Asks Collins to check the tracking light.

demand.title: Coordinate yaw maneuver
demand.interpretation: Offers to begin yaw when it suits Collins.

demand.title: Thruster-use question
demand.interpretation: Asks whether the operation can proceed without thruster use.

demand.title: Repeat high-gain angles
demand.interpretation: Requests the numbers again, then reads back the repeated angles. One episode.

demand.title: Separation pitch question
demand.interpretation: Asks Collins for the pitch angle at separation.

demand.title: Checklist restatement
demand.interpretation: Asks What? and Aldrin restates checklist items.

demand.title: Check ground monitoring
demand.interpretation: Checks that ground is monitoring DELTA-H.

demand.title: Ask for alarm interpretation
demand.interpretation: Requests ground guidance on the 1202 computer alarm. Alarm announcements are grouped, not counted as separate requests.

demand.title: Confirm drift
demand.interpretation: Checks forward drift during landing.

demand.title: Protect immediate task time
demand.interpretation: Tells ground the crew will be busy for a minute.

demand.title: Keep rendezvous support ready
demand.interpretation: Asks Collins to keep the orbiting base ready.

demand.title: Mission timer troubleshooting
demand.interpretation: Reports a timer problem and the results of attempted fixes; one technical issue episode.

demand.title: Confirm position acceptance
demand.interpretation: Asks ground whether to accept the position update.

demand.title: Updated LM weight
demand.interpretation: Requests the updated LM weight.

demand.title: Request block data
demand.interpretation: Invites ground to give the next block of data.

demand.title: Battery voltage concern
demand.interpretation: Reports unequal voltages and asks whether this is expected.

demand.title: Begin powerdown
demand.interpretation: States readiness to power down and terminate the simulated countdown.

demand.title: Update EVA preparation timing
demand.interpretation: Clarifies hatch/preparation timing and later reports the start of EVA preparation. Grouped as one task-plan update.

effort.title: Angle numbers repeated
effort.interpretation: The requested numbers are repeated and read back correctly. This demonstrates a repaired exchange, not cognitive impairment.

effort.title: Checklist restated
effort.interpretation: What? is followed by a checklist restatement. No explicit Armstrong acknowledgment is captured here.

effort.title: Timer reading repeated
effort.interpretation: Ground asks for the timer value again; Armstrong repeats it and ground confirms copying it. This is communication repair, not evidence of confusion.

effort.title: T4 readback corrected
effort.interpretation: The crew read back 07; ground corrected it to 02 and Armstrong read back the correction. The initial error is not attributed to Armstrong alone.

coordination.title: Relay needed repeated numbers
coordination.interpretation: Ground had lost data with Columbia and used Armstrong as a relay. This is an operational coordination snag, not interpersonal conflict.

coordination.title: A shared value needed correction
coordination.interpretation: A wrong shared time value was corrected through readback. The excerpt supports repair work, not a strained relationship.

pressure.title: Busy with immediate tasks
pressure.interpretation: An explicit request for space to perform immediate tasks. It does not by itself mean emotional distress.

pressure.title: Alarms competed with visual attention
pressure.interpretation: Armstrong explicitly says attention to alarms displaced attention to picking out the landing spot. This is the clearest first-person evidence of competing task demands.

support.title: Activation issue received a ground suggestion
support.interpretation: Ground offered a procedure; Armstrong reported finding a misplaced breaker. This does not establish that the ground suggestion solved it.

support.title: Ground interpreted the alarm
support.interpretation: The help request received a GO response, then an acknowledgment. A response is not proof that the alarm was fixed.

support.title: Ground engaged with timer troubleshooting
support.interpretation: Advice was offered and ground said it would research the issue. Timer resolution is not established.

support.title: Ground answered the voltage concern
support.interpretation: Ground answered the concern and Armstrong acknowledged it. This captures support, not an independent medical or system-health assessment.

excerpts.title: Attention pulled in two directions
excerpts.quote: We were a little busy worrying about program alarms and things like that in the part of the descent where we would normally be picking out our landing spot;
excerpts.meaning: You described alarms taking attention away from another important task. That is a clear reason to take the day’s demand seriously.
excerpts.boundary: Evidence of competing attention, not proof of lasting cognitive overload.

excerpts.title: You made room to focus
excerpts.quote: Okay. We're going to be busy for a minute.
excerpts.meaning: You signaled that immediate work needed your attention. Protecting focus is a useful response to demand.
excerpts.boundary: This is an operational boundary, not a sign of distress by itself.

excerpts.title: You used the support around you
excerpts.quote: Give us a reading on the 1202 PROGRAM ALARM.
excerpts.meaning: You asked ground for a clear decision. A reply and your acknowledgment are captured in the exchange.
excerpts.boundary: This shows help-seeking and a response, not that every issue was resolved.

excerpts.title: There was a positive moment, too
excerpts.quote: It's big and bright and beautiful.
excerpts.meaning: Even amid the procedures, you noticed a positive view of Earth. The day contained more than demand.
excerpts.boundary: A positive description is not a measure of your overall mood.

recommendations.title: Protect your next agreed pause
recommendations.text: When the mission plan allows, take a short quiet pause before adding another noncritical task. Let ground know you need that space.
recommendations.why: You described competing demands and asked for a minute to focus.

recommendations.title: Share a short debrief with Buzz
recommendations.text: Talk through what took the most effort and what helped. Keep it practical: one demanding moment, one useful support, one thing to simplify.
recommendations.why: A few exchanges needed restatement or correction; support also worked.

recommendations.title: Keep the next optional block simple
recommendations.text: Ask to group nonurgent questions or defer an optional task. Keep required checks and mission decisions with the crew and ground team.
recommendations.why: Technical decisions and troubleshooting continued after landing.

recommendations.title: Protect rest after operations
recommendations.text: When operations and the agreed plan permit, preserve your rest opportunity. Use your own check-in to say whether you still feel switched on or depleted.
recommendations.why: A demanding task sequence is a reason to plan recovery. This source contains no measured sleep data.

baseline.label: Demo personal baseline
baseline.description: Illustrative usual ranges for the same reviewed episode definitions. These are not extracted from Neil Armstrong’s historical days. Today’s transcript entries and reviewed episode counts remain real-source based.
